Simulation-convergence status of a calibration (green / yellow / red)

Source: R/calc_convergence_status.R
calc_convergence_status.Rd

Four checks, each coloured green, yellow or red; the overall status is the worst of them.

CheckGreenYellowRed
Ensemble ESS (ess_best)\(\ge\) target\(\ge\) 0.5 x targetbelow
Monte Carlo error (mce_p90)\(\le\) 0.10\(\le\) 0.15above
Validity guard (khat)< 0.5< 0.7\(\ge\) 0.7
Data informativeness (ess_untempered_frac)< 0.01\(\ge\) 0.01 (flat likelihood)–

  • Ensemble ESS: the Kish ESS of the best-fit ensemble. The Monte Carlo standard error of a posterior mean is about SD / \(\sqrt{ESS}\), so 7 percent of the posterior SD at 200 and 10 percent at 100.

  • Monte Carlo error: the 90th percentile over parameters of the seed-batch standard error of the ensemble's posterior means, in posterior SDs (Flegal & Jones 2010). It is a standard error: two independent reruns differ by about \(\sqrt{2}\) times it (SD). The true value is nearly the same for every parameter (about \(1/\sqrt{ESS_{best}}\)), so the spread over parameters is mostly estimation noise and the 90th percentile is a conservative summary (about 1.3 times the typical value).

  • Validity guard: Pareto k-hat of the tempered importance weights (Vehtari et al. 2024). The tempered weights are bounded, so the true tail shape is \(\le 0\) and k-hat falls as draws accumulate; a high value means a few draws carry much of the weight at this number of draws. The reason states the k-hat trend (khat_trend): when falling, the simulations at which it would reach 0.5 at that rate and whether that is within max_simulations; "uncertain" when the trend is within twice its standard error of zero. An undefined k-hat is green only when the tail ratios are tied (weights nearly flat, khat_cause containing "tied"); any other cause is yellow, "not assessed".

  • Data informativeness: the Kish ESS of the untempered (\(\eta = 1\)) likelihood weights as a share of the valid draws. With informative data it collapses to about \(1/N\); a share of at least thresholds$flat_ess_frac (default 0.01) means the likelihood is flat over a sizeable part of the prior, so the posterior is close to the prior. The share does not depend on the number of draws. The sampling can be adequate while the result is uninformative, so it is yellow, never red. A flat verdict also needs an untempered Kish ESS of at least 20: the share is at least \(1/N\), so on a small run a collapsed likelihood (ESS 1-3) would otherwise read as flat. It is not assessed (yellow) with fewer than two valid draws. Many draws tied at the best log-likelihood (a plateau, at least 10) add a note to the reason, and an undefined k-hat from too few distinct tail ratios then counts as tied.

A run with fewer than two valid draws has failed: its first reason says so (no posterior can be formed and more simulations of the same setup will not help) and every check reads "not assessed".

Missing values in the other checks are never green: an NA ess_best is red (no ensemble), an NA mce_p90 is yellow ("not assessed"). An infinite mce_p90 (fewer than two seed batches hold members) is red.

Every non-green check contributes one plain-language reason naming its remedy. The ESS reason quotes the draws projected to reach the target, \(N \times ESS_{all}^{target} / ESS_{all}\) (supply n_draws, ess_all and ess_all_target, or n_draws_projected); the Monte Carlo error reason uses MCE \(\propto 1/\sqrt{N}\). Both are converted from valid draws to simulations at the run's success rate (n_draws / n_attempted). A projection is reliable only when the ESS growth slope is known and at least thresholds$slope_stall; every reason that quotes one says so otherwise.

Flags never change the colour: budget_cap_reached, ess_growth_stalled (slope below thresholds$slope_stall), ensemble_size_bound (a member bound set the ensemble size) and fixed_budget (the status is assessed, not used to stop).

The function is pure (no I/O, no RNG) and takes scalars; apply it across runs with lapply() / Map().

Usage

calc_convergence_status(
  ess_best,
  ess_best_target = 200,
  mce_p90,
  khat,
  flat = NA,
  ess_all = NA_real_,
  ess_all_target = NA_real_,
  n_draws = NA_real_,
  n_draws_projected = NA_real_,
  slope = NA_real_,
  budget_exhausted = FALSE,
  fixed_mode = FALSE,
  size_bound = NA_character_,
  eta_star = NA_real_,
  thresholds = list(),
  ess_untempered_frac = NA_real_,
  n_tied_max = NA_real_,
  khat_cause = NA_character_,
  khat_trend = NA_character_,
  khat_trend_slope = NA_real_,
  n_attempted = NA_real_,
  max_simulations = NA_real_,
  batch_size_min = 500,
  batch_size_max = 10000
)

Arguments

ess_best

Kish ESS of the best-fit ensemble.

ess_best_target

Required ensemble ESS (control$targets$ESS_best). Default 200.

mce_p90

90th percentile over parameters of the members' Monte Carlo error / posterior SD.

khat

Pareto k-hat of the tempered weights (NA = undefined).

flat

Optional logical flat-likelihood verdict, used only when ess_untempered_frac is NA.

ess_all

Optional Kish ESS of the posterior over all draws.

ess_all_target

Optional ESS_all target (ess_best_target / best_subset_ratio).

n_draws

Optional valid draws (finite log-likelihood) so far.

n_draws_projected

Optional total valid draws projected to reach the ESS target; computed from n_draws, ess_all and ess_all_target when NA.

slope

Optional log-log ESS growth slope over the latter part of the run.

budget_exhausted

Logical; the run stopped at max_simulations_total.

fixed_mode

Logical; a fixed-budget run.

size_bound

Which bound set the ensemble size: "ratio", "min_members", "max_members" (or NA).

eta_star

Optional supported resolution \(\eta^*\) (a diagnostic; not used by the rule).

thresholds

Named list overriding the band thresholds: ess_yellow_frac (0.5), mce_green (0.10), mce_yellow (0.15), khat_green (0.5), khat_yellow (0.7), slope_stall (0.8), flat_ess_frac (0.01).

ess_untempered_frac

Optional Kish ESS of the untempered (\(\eta = 1\)) weights / valid draws.

n_tied_max

Optional number of valid draws tied at the best log-likelihood.

khat_cause

Optional reason k-hat is undefined (the calc_is_diagnostics() khat_status).

khat_trend

Optional "falling", "not falling" or "uncertain": k-hat over growing numbers of draws (.mosaic_khat_trend()).

khat_trend_slope

Optional change of k-hat per doubling of the draws, quoted when k-hat is falling.

n_attempted

Optional simulations attempted (valid or not); converts projected valid draws to simulations.

max_simulations

Optional simulation budget (max_simulations_total); the k-hat reason says whether its projection is within it.

batch_size_min, batch_size_max

Bounds of the confirming batch in sims_projected_for_green (batch_size_adaptive, max_batch_predictive). Defaults 500 and 10,000.

Value

A list with

status

"green", "yellow" or "red".

label

The status text: "Converged: enough simulations", "Usable with caution" or "Not converged: more simulations needed".

checks

Data frame, one row per check (check is "ess", "mce", "khat" or "informativeness"): label, value, threshold_green, threshold_yellow (NA for the informativeness check), colour and reason.

reasons

Character vector, one reason per non-green check.

flags

Character vector of flag identifiers, zero or more of "budget_cap_reached", "ess_growth_stalled", "ensemble_size_bound" and "fixed_budget" (summary.json schema 2 convergence_flags).

flag_text

Character vector parallel to flags: the plain-language text of each flag (joined into convergence_flags_text).

n_draws_projected, n_draws_more

Projected total valid draws for the ESS target and the shortfall (NA when unknown).

sims_projected_for_green

Total simulations projected for GREEN (units: simulations): the larger of the ESS and Monte Carlo error projections that exceed the current valid draws, divided by the success rate, plus, in adaptive mode, one confirming batch (a quarter of that total within [batch_size_min, batch_size_max]: the second green check of the stopping rule; a fixed-budget run has none); NA when the three sampling checks are green or when no check that more draws can fix is behind.

projection_reliable

FALSE when the growth slope is unknown or below thresholds$slope_stall.

success_rate

n_draws / n_attempted (1 when unknown).

sampling_green

TRUE when the three sampling checks (ensemble ESS, Monte Carlo error, k-hat) are green, whatever the informativeness check: the adaptive stopping condition.

flat

The flat-likelihood verdict (NA when not assessed).

thresholds

The thresholds used.

Details

Answers one question: are there enough simulations to represent the model's best-fitting ensemble reliably? The status is the single rule behind the adaptive stopping gate, summary.json, the calibration report and the backfill (calc_run_weight_health). Whether the model fits the data (R², bias, coverage) is reported elsewhere and never enters it.

References

Vehtari A, Gelman A, Simpson D, Carpenter B, Bürkner P-C (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: an improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC. Bayesian Analysis 16(2):667-718.

Vehtari A, Simpson D, Gelman A, Yao Y, Gabry J (2024). Pareto smoothed importance sampling. JMLR 25(72):1-58.

Flegal JM, Jones GL (2010). Batch means and spectral variance estimators in Markov chain Monte Carlo. Annals of Statistics 38(2):1034-1070.

See also

calc_weight_health, calc_run_weight_health

Other calibration-metrics: calc_convergence_diagnostics(), calc_model_agreement_index(), calc_model_cvw(), calc_model_ess(), calc_run_weight_health(), calc_weight_health()

Examples

st <- calc_convergence_status(ess_best = 140, ess_best_target = 200,
                              mce_p90 = 0.08, khat = 0.2,
                              ess_untempered_frac = 2e-5,
                              ess_all = 700, ess_all_target = 1000,
                              n_draws = 50000, slope = 0.98)
st$status
#> [1] "yellow"
st$reasons
#> [1] "ensemble ESS 140 of 200: about 21k more simulations would reach the target"
st$checks
#>             check                               label   value threshold_green
#> 1             ess                        Ensemble ESS 1.4e+02           2e+02
#> 2             mce Monte Carlo error (90th percentile) 8.0e-02           1e-01
#> 3            khat       Validity guard (Pareto k-hat) 2.0e-01           5e-01
#> 4 informativeness                Data informativeness 2.0e-05           1e-02
#>   threshold_yellow colour
#> 1           100.00 yellow
#> 2             0.15  green
#> 3             0.70  green
#> 4               NA  green
#>                                                                                                                  reason
#> 1                                            ensemble ESS 140 of 200: about 21k more simulations would reach the target
#> 2 Monte Carlo standard error of the posterior means 8.0% of the posterior SD (90th percentile over parameters) <= 10.0%
#> 3                                                                       Pareto k-hat of the tempered weights 0.20 < 0.5
#> 4                            the data inform the posterior (the untempered likelihood ESS is 0.002% of the draws, < 1%)
